title: Robbing Peter to Pay Paul: The Impact of California’s Cap-and-Trade Program on Toxic Emissions
eligible_reason: Single adoption date and continuous treatment. The headline regressor 'stringency' (inverse of industry-wide free allowances per facility) is continuous; the one binary specification, CA_after2013 (Table 2), switches on for all California cap-and-trade facilities in 2013, i.e. one adoption cohort versus never-treated matched facilities. Every column also includes time-varying controls (max_chem, since_inspection, since_EPA_action), matching weights and facility and year FE (xtreg fe, cluster state). Figure 2 uses eventdd with timeToTreat = year - 2014 for CA facilities, again a single date. Fails the at-least-two-adoption-cohorts rule, so it is not a near-miss either.
design_notes: MSFT2023_03560Code.do: xtset newid year; Table 2 loop (line 30-32) over stringency / auction / CA_after2013: xtreg log_Toxic `j' max_chem since_inspection since_EPA_action i.year [weight=weight], fe cluster(state), if sample==1. Panel 2010-2018, 1,044 facilities, 8,239 facility-years in the replication data. Table 3-4: mechanisms and splits with the continuous stringency. The shipped data omit D&B variables (employees, owner information), so the README warns results differ from the paper.
